Actor: section 10 of the Railway Labor Act as restated by this order. The order was functionally spent on 1967-06-11.

clauses.mechanism: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; 51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:", in a two-column table headed 'No. Subject'; its entry "11343 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute" names this order by number. A scan of the full held text of EO 12553 for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects (the words effectiveness and Suspending), not as operative wording, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, 1986-02-25; that is an inference from the heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate three disputes between The Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, bars interested members, directs a report "within 30 days from the date of this order." and restates the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11343 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute"). Later events, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the board reported by a letter of transmittal dated May 12, 1967 (held NMB copy of the report), and the standstill ran out on June 11, 1967 (inclusive reading; exclusive alternative stated in the event). The order was functionally spent on 1967-06-11 and remained in force until revoked. The order states no end date of its own, and the by-number scan of held order texts finds no later order citing it.

research_rationale:
EO 11343 (signed 1967-04-12; 32 FR 6085, Federal Register of April 18, 1967) creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate three disputes between The Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers; bars members interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; directs the board to report "within 30 days from the date of this order."; and restates the section 10 standstill, under which no change except by agreement may be made in the conditions out of which the disputes arose "from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report" to the President. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11343.txt, PDF page 5); its number, title and the April 18, 1967 issue line match the census register row, but the extracted text prints no page number, so I did not confirm the page 6085 citation from it. The order has one operative paragraph group with no numbered sections, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number in its table; that express revocation is the first end. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the board's report and the end of the standstill are spent facts recorded as later events: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11343_Emergency_Board_report_to_the_President_on_the_Long_Island_Rail_Road_disputes_EO_1134_fc0b3e43ef.txt; PDF file sha256 5a7a3638cdd0d3d0614bcc0f37e5ddb86cab8e4c2c5f0fdae6e72565c2104a71) is the Report to the President by Emergency Board No. 170 appointed by EO 11343, with a letter of transmittal dated May 12, 1967, so the standstill ran through June 11, 1967. The order was functionally spent on 1967-06-11 and stayed on the books until EO 12553. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters); and a read of the report's front matter and letter of transmittal (PDF pages 1-3).

savings.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception or pending-matter wording: a scan of its full held text for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects. Its revocation leaves nothing of this order in operation. The board's creation, its report of May 12, 1967 and the standstill that ended on June 11, 1967 are completed facts, not continuing commands. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1967-06-11 counts thirty days from the transmittal date and is recorded inclusive (the standstill runs through that day); the exclusive reading ends it at the start of 1967-06-11. If the report reached the President after the date on its transmittal letter, the standstill ended correspondingly later.
source_notes.reason: Functionally spent on 1967-06-11: the board reported by a letter of transmittal dated May 12, 1967 (held NMB copy of the report, PDF pages 1 and 3), and the standstill this sentence restates ran for thirty days after the report. The order nevertheless remained in force until its express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadlines).
